faqs.q: What is the Dixon Hydraulic 4-Bolt Flanges, NPTF Port used for?
faqs.a: The Dixon Hydraulic 4-Bolt Flanges, NPTF Port are SAE four-bolt hydraulic flanges in carbon steel with a NPTF female port, used to connect a hose, tube or port to a flanged line. The listing has 28 part numbers in Code 61 and Code 62, as O-ring flanges and flat-face flanges. See the [SAE flanges shelf](/c/hydraulic-sae-flanges).

faqs.q: How do I read Dixon flange part numbers such as C6143K0808NPT and C6244K0808NPT?
faqs.a: In the rows the first three characters give the flange code: C61 is Code 61 and C62 is Code 62. The last three letters, NPT, give the port type, and the digits before them show the size as a pair of dash sizes, such as 0808 for a 1/2" size. The characters between them mark the flange style.

faqs.q: Which sizes do the Dixon Hydraulic 4-Bolt Flanges, NPTF Port come in?
faqs.a: The part numbers in this listing run through dash sizes 08 to 48, starting at the 1/2" size, with Code 61 flanges listed in 16 part numbers and Code 62 in 12. The size is in the part number as a dash size, where 08 is the 1/2" size. Quote the code, size and port thread.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Code 61 and Code 62 in the Dixon Hydraulic 4-Bolt Flanges, NPTF Port?
faqs.a: Code 61 and Code 62 are the SAE J518 flange series: the shelf lists Code 61 at 210 bar and Code 62 at 415 bar. In this listing 16 part numbers are Code 61 (such as C6143K0808NPT) and 12 are Code 62 (such as C6244K0808NPT). Flanges of different codes do not mix, so match the code of your port.

faqs.q: What pressure are the Dixon Hydraulic 4-Bolt Flanges, NPTF Port rated for?
faqs.a: The Dixon rows do not publish a pressure rating, and the shelf states Code 61 at 210 bar and Code 62 at 415 bar for the SAE J518 series. The rating of a flange decreases as its size increases, so confirm the figure for your size with us before ordering, and note that the joint is only as strong as the bolts, O-ring and flange together.

faqs.q: What are O-rings for SAE hydraulic flanges used for?
faqs.a: These are spare face O-rings for SAE J518 four-bolt flange connections, Code 61 and Code 62, in sizes 1/2" to 5". faqs.q: How do I choose between Code 61 and Code 62 O-rings?
faqs.a: Choose by the flange code of your port, which is marked on the flange or its part number; Code 61 is standard pressure and Code 62 is high pressure. The two codes have different groove dimensions at the same nominal size, so quote the code with the size.

faqs.q: What pressure rating do SAE flange O-rings have?
faqs.a: None of its own: the listing says the O-ring does not set the pressure rating of the joint, which comes from the flange, its code and the bolts. What the O-ring decides is whether the joint stays dry, so use a new, undamaged ring of the right compound.

faqs.q: What compound are O-rings for SAE hydraulic flanges made of?
faqs.a: The listing gives the material as elastomer, with the compound matched to the fluid and temperature. Nitrile suits mineral hydraulic oil at ordinary temperatures, and fluorocarbon (FKM) is the usual step up for higher temperatures and many synthetic fluids. Tell us the fluid, temperature and pressure.

faqs.q: Which standard do O-rings for SAE hydraulic flanges follow?

faqs.q: Can I re-use an SAE flange O-ring, and how do I fit it?
faqs.a: Fit a new O-ring every time the flange is broken: a used ring has taken a set in its groove and may not seal again. Clean the groove and face, lightly lubricate the ring with system fluid, and draw the bolts up evenly in a cross pattern so the ring is not pinched out.

faqs.q: Why does an SAE four-bolt flange weep and is it the O-ring?
faqs.a: A flange that weeps is more often a flattened, nicked or wrong-compound O-ring, or one pinched out of its groove at assembly, than a fault in the flange itself. Replace the ring first, checking the face for scratches across the sealing area; see [reading a weeping joint](/blog/reading-a-weeping-joint).
